customers.name: The Pragmatist
customers.surface_mood: Neutral, clipped. Already checking the time.
customers.bizard_flavor: Just tell me what it does.
customers.design_note: Easy to read, easy to please if you stay out of their way. The trap is trying to warm them up.

customers.name: The Softie
customers.surface_mood: Warm, open, possibly nervous. Makes eye contact, then looks away.
customers.bizard_flavor: Oh, it just... spoke to me, you know?
customers.design_note: Easy sell if handled gently. Aggressive close loses them completely.

customers.name: The Skeptic
customers.surface_mood: Arms crossed. Possibly squinting. Not hostile — just unconvinced.
customers.design_note: Patience pays off. Rushing them or hyping them = instant lost sale.

customers.name: The Wildcard
customers.surface_mood: Impossible to read. Could be anything. Currently staring at the ceiling.
customers.bizard_flavor: I'll take three. Actually no. Tell me about the other one.
customers.design_note: High Charm smooths the variance. Low Charm is genuinely a coin flip. The most memorable customer in the game.

customers.name: The Overthinker
customers.surface_mood: Anxious, apologetic, slightly sweaty. Already second-guessing being here.
customers.bizard_flavor: But what if I need the other one? Is this the right one? How do I know?
customers.design_note: Never rush. Never decide for them. Guide, don't push.

customers.name: The Expert
customers.surface_mood: Calm, slightly smug. Has done the research. Knows things. Wants you to know that.
customers.bizard_flavor: I've actually read quite a bit about this.
customers.design_note: The trap is over-explaining. They know. Acknowledge it.

customers.name: The Haggler
customers.surface_mood: Immediately suspicious. Wallet already tightening. Eyes scanning for the price tag.
customers.design_note: The sale outcome ceiling is lower with this customer. They will never pay full.

customers.name: The Venter
customers.surface_mood: Visibly frustrated. Not at you. Probably. Sighing before they speak.
customers.bizard_flavor: Sorry, it's just been a day. A week. A year, honestly.
customers.design_note: Hard gate on early stages. Player who skips straight to selling loses them before Stage 3.

customers.name: The Distracted One
customers.surface_mood: Elsewhere mentally. Phone probably out. Nodding at things you haven't said yet.
customers.bizard_flavor: Sorry, what? Yeah. Sure. Wait, what does it do again?
customers.design_note: Window of attention is short. Land it fast or lose them to their phone.

customers.name: The Entitled One
customers.surface_mood: Cool, expectant. Already slightly disappointed. Somehow.
customers.bizard_flavor: I shop here a lot, you know. (First visit.)
customers.design_note: Ego management from Stage 1. Never joke. Never push back.

customers.name: The Gusher
customers.surface_mood: Extremely enthusiastic. Already loves it. Possibly already named it.
customers.bizard_flavor: I already know I want it I just need you to tell me it's okay.
customers.design_note: The trap archetype. Players see enthusiasm and mirror it. Wrong call. They needed confirmation, not a pitch.

customers.name: The Guilty Buyer
customers.surface_mood: Sheepish, slightly furtive. Glancing toward the door periodically.
customers.bizard_flavor: My partner doesn't know I'm here.
customers.design_note: Keep it light. They know what they're doing. Don't make it a whole thing.

customers.name: The Browser
customers.surface_mood: Relaxed, no urgency whatsoever. Handling items they have no intention of buying.
customers.design_note: Patient, low-pressure play can convert them. Rushing guarantees a walkout.

customers.name: The Comparison Shopper
customers.surface_mood: Analytical, slightly distracted by internal calculations. Has a spreadsheet. Mentally.
customers.bizard_flavor: How does this compare to the one down the road?
customers.design_note: Answer the question. Don't redirect. Don't embellish.

customers.name: The Returner
customers.surface_mood: Resigned, slightly defeated. Already holding the item they want to exchange.
customers.bizard_flavor: I just want something that works.
customers.design_note: Low mood ceiling. Best outcome is a clean even or small profit. Don't push for the big close.

customers.name: The Silent One
customers.surface_mood: Completely unreadable. Nodding. You have no idea if that's good.
customers.bizard_flavor: (Nods. You have no idea if that's good.)
customers.design_note: Hardest read in the game. High Charm players survive it. Low Charm players are guessing every stage.

customers.name: The Kid's Parent
customers.surface_mood: Frazzled, distracted, running on fumes. Child either present or recently escaped.
customers.bizard_flavor: My kid said it was magic. Is it magic? Great. How much?
customers.design_note: Fastest possible sale if you match their pace. Slow them down and they check out entirely.
